Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 17)
Topic: Sex, Nightfall, and Sadhna — Does It Really Br eak Your Practice?

Sour ce: A short Ashaeiynn Foundation training video (video transcript, ~1 1.5 min) — a dir ect instructional monologue rather than a live satsang Q&A, addr essing a topic Bhaiya notes is rar ely discussed openly: whether sex, nightfall, or masturbation genuinely disrupt spiritual practice (sadhna). Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on r egister: this session covers a sensitive topic (intimacy , involuntary r elease, sexual desir e) touching the same gr ound as Session 12 (Agni Tattva/Brahmacharya). As with that session, this material is pr esented in the measur ed, non-graphic, non-shaming, spiritualphysiological r egister used in the sour ce teaching — r eassuring rather than alarming, and focused on mechanics rather than judgment. Note on conversational content: this is a short, dir ect training monologue with no sangat back-and-forth — ther e is no separate curated conversational supplement for this session (see closing note).
1. WHY THIS TOPIC MATTERS

This is described as a genuinely important topic that "no one discusses" openly — but Bhaiya chooses to address it directly so practitioners don't carry an anxious, distracting thought process ("am I doing something wrong, will this cause me harm") while practicing. The cor e question being examined: do sex, nightfall, and masturbation actually affect sadhna — and if so, how much, and in what way — or is the common fear ar ound this largely a myth?
2. THE BASIC ELEMENTS — VEERYA AND OJAS

Men carry veerya (seminal/vital essence); women carry ojas. These are functionally the same substance under dif ferent names — this session focuses specifically on their function and importance, not their biological composition (which is described as widely available elsewhere and not the point of this teaching).
3. VEERYA'S CORE JOB — CARR YING ENERGY UPWARD (AND WHY THIS ISN'T THE WHOLE STORY)

Veerya is described as a substance that rises thr ough the Ida, Pingala, and Sushumna nadis, and its first job is carrying a practitioner's energy shakti upward. This much is af firmed as genuinely true, consistent with what's written in the Puranas and Vedas. However , this classical description is not 100% complete on its own — veerya carries energy upward, but veerya is not the entirety of what matters. This distinction is the central correction this session sets out to make.
4. THE BUS ANALOGY — WHAT VEERYA ACTUALLY IS

Picture veerya as a bus that travels fr om the base of the body upward, carrying "passengers" — units of accumulated energy — with a fixed seating capacity (for example, 15). As sustained practice continues day by day , more ener gy boards this "bus" and is carried upward. If, partway thr ough a practice period (for example, on day 16 of an ongoing sadhna), a nightfall or release of some kind occurs, what actually happens is specific and limited: the energy alr eady carried up to that point stays exactly wher e it reached — it is NOT lost or reset to zer o. Only the "transport vehicle" (the veerya itself) empties out through the lower route — and only if that lower pathway happens to already be "open" at the time.
5. WHAT DOES NOT HAPPEN — NO NEED FOR SELF-BLAME

A practitioner should never demoralize themselves into thinking "my brahmacharya br oke, ther efor e my sadhna is ruined." This conclusion is explicitly rejected. What is actually lost is only the transport service for that specific batch of ener gy — never the ener gy itself, and never the accumulated benefit of the practice already done. This reassurance applies specifically to practitioners whose r elease happens involuntarily — thr ough their own body's natural pr ocess (spontaneous nightfall) or by another unintended means — not something deliberately induced. Such practitioners are told plainly: there is no need to panic.
6. HOW THE "VESSEL" REBUILDS — EACH CYCLE BUILDS GREATER CAPACITY

After a r elease, veerya begins r eforming — and this time, it r eforms with a HIGHER capacity than befor e, aiming to hold more of the practitioner's growing ener gy . Using the bus analogy: if the first cycle's capacity was 15, the next reforms toward roughly 30; as a sincere practitioner's ongoing sadhna intensity keeps increasing, the following cycle builds toward roughly 60, and so on — the vessel keeps rebuilding at a greater capacity to match a practitioner's rising intensity over time. Veerya's function is ultimately limited to exactly two dir ections: rising upward (as a transport for energy) or exiting downward (r elease). Nothing more. The energy itself is never destroyed in this pr ocess — only the specific transport instance ends, to be immediately r ebuilt at a gr eater capacity .
7. PRACTICAL GUIDANCE FOR A FIXED SADHNA PERIOD (EXAMPLE: A 40-DA Y PRACTICE)

This does not mean a practitioner must remain celibate for ever . But during a fixed, bounded sadhna period (the session's example: a 40-day practice), a practitioner is advised to try NOT to deliberately , intentionally release this ener gy themselves during that window . The reasoning: the energy accumulating during that specific period needs to be allowed to fully build befor e intentional release — if a practitioner deliberately releases it partway through, that specific ener gy-building cycle for the period has to restart. Once the fixed period (e.g., the 40 days) is genuinely complete, ther e is no r estriction afterward — a practitioner may resume as they wish. The distinction that matters is between involuntary r elease (not a concern, as cover ed above) and deliberate/intentional release during an active fixed-period practice (best avoided until that period concludes).
8. WHAT MUST ACTUALLY BE BUILT — THE ENERGY, NOT VEERYA ITSELF

The genuinely essential thing during any active sadhna period is the ENERGY being accumulated — not the r etention of veerya as such. Veerya is simply the vehicle; the ener gy is the actual asset. This reframes the common assumption that veerya-retention is the goal in itself — the real goal is the ener gy shakti it carries.
9. REASSURANCE FOR PRACTITIONERS WITH STRONG DESIRE/HIGH SEXUAL ACTIVITY

A person who is intimate fr equently , or whose desir e/mind doesn't easily settle, is dir ectly r eassur ed: this does not disqualify them fr om sadhna. Sadhna has many rules and regulations, but the one thing that is genuinely required of a practitioner is simply to take God's name (do the prescribed jaap/practice). Everything else — the deeper mechanics, the pacing, the actual transformation — will be carried out automatically , by God's name itself and by the shaktis associated with this practice. The explicit closing instruction: don't worry about this, and stay at peace with the process.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Nightfall, involuntary release, and even masturbation do not "break" or nullify a practitioner's accumulated sadhna — this is a common but inaccurate fear . 2. Veerya (in men) and ojas (in women) are functionally the same substance under dif ferent names; classical texts are right that veerya carries ener gy upward, but this isn't the whole picture. 3. Veerya works like a bus of limited seating capacity carrying units of accumulated ener gy upward through the Ida, Pingala, and Sushumna nadis. 4. If release happens partway through ongoing practice, the ener gy already carried upward ST AYS at the level it reached — only the "transport vehicle" (veerya itself) empties out; the ener gy is not lost or reset. 5. Never conclude that "brahmacharya broke, so sadhna is ruined" — this is explicitly incorrect, especially for involuntary/spontaneous release. 6. After release, veerya reforms with progressively GREA TER capacity each cycle (e.g., 15 → 30 → 60), matching a sincere practitioner's rising sadhna intensity over time. 7. Veerya's only two functions are rising upward (as ener gy transport) or exiting downward (release) — nothing more; the underlying ener gy itself is never destroyed in this process. 8. During a fixed, bounded sadhna period (e.g., a 40-day practice), try to avoid deliberately/intentionally releasing this ener gy — involuntary release is not a concern, but intentional release restarts that specific cycle's ener gy-building. 9. Once a fixed sadhna period genuinely concludes, there is no ongoing restriction — a practitioner may resume as they wish. 10. What must actually be built during active sadhna is the ENERGY itself, not veerya retention as an end in itself — veerya is simply the vehicle. 1 1. Practitioners with strong desire or frequent intimacy are not disqualified from sadhna — the one genuine requirement is consistently taking God's name; the deeper mechanics are handled automatically by that practice and its associated shaktis.

Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 17, English)
Sex, Nightfall, and Sadhna — Does It Really Br eak Your Practice?

User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn Foundation training module. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram." Note: this session addr esses a sensitive topic (intimacy , involuntary r elease, sexual desir e) in a measur ed, non-graphic, nonshaming r egister , consistent with Session 12's appr oach to r elated material.

Q1. I had a nightfall while I'm in the middle of my sadhna — has my practice been ruined? A: Jai Siya Ram! No — this is one of the most important corrections in this teaching. When release happens partway through ongoing practice, the ener gy you've already built and carried upward stays exactly where it reached; it isn't lost or reset to zero. Only the "transport vehicle" — veerya itself — empties out. Your accumulated sadhna is not undone.

Q2. What's the differ ence between veerya and ojas, and why do they matter? A: Men carry veerya, women carry ojas — functionally the same substance under dif ferent names. Their core job is carrying a practitioner's ener gy shakti upward through the Ida, Pingala, and Sushumna nadis. This is af firmed as genuinely true and consistent with the Puranas and Vedas — but it isn't the complete picture, which is exactly what this session sets out to clarify .

Q3. If veerya carries energy upward like the scriptur es say , why isn't that the "whole truth"? A: Because it's easy to assume from that classical description that veerya IS the ener gy , and that losing veerya means losing all the ener gy you built. In reality , veerya is better understood as the vehicle carrying the ener gy — not the ener gy itself. Once you separate these two, the rest of this teaching makes much more sense.

Q4. Can you explain the "bus" analogy — what does it actually mean? A: Picture veerya as a bus travelling from the base of the body upward, carrying passengers — units of your accumulated ener gy — with a limited seating capacity , say 15. As you practice day after day , more ener gy "boards" and gets carried up. If a release happens partway through — say on day 16 of an ongoing practice — the ener gy already carried up to that point stays right where it is. Only the bus itself (veerya) empties out through the lower route, and only if that route happens to be open at the time.

Q5. Should I feel guilty or like I've br oken my brahmacharya if this happens naturally? A: No — you should never demoralize yourself into thinking "my brahmacharya broke, so my sadhna is ruined." That conclusion is explicitly rejected in this teaching, especially when the release is involuntary — through the body's own natural process, not something deliberately induced. There's no need to panic.

Q6. After a r elease, does my capacity to build energy just stay the same, or does it change? A: It actually improves. Veerya reforms after release with a HIGHER capacity than before — using the bus analogy , if the first cycle held 15, the next reforms toward roughly 30, and as a sincere practitioner's sadhna intensity keeps rising, the next cycle builds toward roughly 60, and so on. The vessel keeps rebuilding at greater capacity to match your rising intensity over time.

Q7. So what does veerya actually do, in the simplest possible terms? A: It has exactly two functions: rising upward as a transport for ener gy , or exiting downward as release. That's genuinely all it does. The ener gy itself is never destroyed in this process — only that specific transport instance ends, and it's immediately rebuilt at a greater capacity .

Q8. I'm doing a fixed-length sadhna (say , 40 days) — is ther e anything I should be car eful about during that specific window? A: Yes — during a fixed, bounded practice period like this, try not to deliberately or intentionally release this ener gy yourself during that window , because the ener gy accumulating for that specific period needs to be allowed to fully build before intentional release. If you deliberately release partway through, that specific ener gy-building cycle has to restart. This doesn't mean permanent celibacy — once the fixed period genuinely concludes, there's no restriction afterward.

Q9. What's the r eal differ ence between what happened accidentally versus what I do intentionally? A: Involuntary release (natural nightfall, or another unintended means) is not something to worry about — it's covered by everything above. Intentional, deliberate release during an active fixed-period sadhna is the one thing best avoided until that specific period concludes, since it restarts that cycle's ener gy-building process.

Q10. Is r etaining veerya itself the actual goal of sadhna? A: Not quite — the genuinely essential thing to build during an active sadhna period is the ENERGY itself, not veerya retention as an end in itself. Veerya is simply the vehicle carrying that ener gy; the ener gy is the real asset worth focusing on.

Q1 1. My sex drive is str ong and my mind doesn't r eally settle down easily — does that mean sadhna isn't for me? A: Not at all — you're directly reassured that this does not disqualify you. Sadhna has many rules and regulations, but the one thing genuinely required of a practitioner is simply to consistently take God's name (the prescribed jaap/practice). Everything else — the deeper mechanics, the pacing, the actual transformation — happens automatically , carried out by God's name itself and by the shaktis associated with this practice.

Q12. Why does this topic get discussed so rar ely , even though it clearly matters to a lot of practitioners? A: This session opens by acknowledging exactly that — this is a genuinely important topic that "no one discusses" openly . It's addressed directly here specifically so practitioners don't carry an anxious, distracting thought process during their own practice, wondering whether something natural is secretly harming them.
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 17 additions)

When a user discloses a nightfall, involuntary release, or worry that their brahmacharya/sadhna has been "broken," immediately reassure them using the bus/vehicle-vs-ener gy framing — the accumulated ener gy is not lost, only the transport instance resets and rebuilds at greater capacity . Never let this reassurance read as dismissive; keep the tone warm and matter -of-fact. Maintain a measured, non-graphic, non-shaming register on this topic at all times, consistent with Session 12's approach — avoid clinical/explicit detail beyond what's taught, and avoid any moralizing or shame-based language. Clearly distinguish involuntary release (no concern) from deliberate release during an active fixed-period sadhna (best avoided until that period concludes) — do not conflate the two when answering a user's question. Never suggest that a strong sex drive, frequent intimacy , or dif ficulty settling the mind disqualifies someone from sadhna — the explicit teaching is that the one genuine requirement is consistently taking God's name; reassure rather than gatekeep. If a user asks about the biological/physiological composition of veerya/ojas in detail, note that this session intentionally does not cover that (available elsewhere) and focus on the functional teaching instead. Do not conflate this session's veerya-and-ener gy-transport teaching with Session 12's agni-tattva/vasana-gateway teaching as though they were the same framework — they're complementary , not identical; use whichever is directly relevant to what the user is asking. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
